Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.

# Green Party Manifesto 2024 Summary

The Green Party presents its manifesto against the backdrop of a cost-of-living crisis and escalating climate emergency, arguing that Britain—despite its wealth—fails its citizens through crumbling public services, unaffordable housing, and inadequate healthcare. The party promises transformative change through principled political choices.

## Climate and Energy

Climate action forms the manifesto's foundation. The Greens commit to transitioning to zero-carbon far ahead of 2050, with wind providing 70% of electricity by 2030. They would ban new fossil fuel extraction, cancel recent licences like Rosebank, end oil and gas subsidies, and introduce a carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne. Nuclear power would be phased out as expensive and unnecessary. Community ownership of renewable energy infrastructure would be mandated, ensuring local communities benefit from the green transition.

## Economic Transformation

The party proposes £40 billion annually in green investment, covering electricity generation, building retrofitting, railway electrification, and public transport. Privatised utilities—railways, water companies, and major energy retailers—would return to public ownership. A wealth tax on assets exceeding £10 million, reformed capital gains tax, and aligned taxation on all income sources would fund public services, raising an estimated £50-70 billion annually.

## Health and Social Care

The NHS would receive £28 billion additional annual funding by 2030, alongside £20 billion capital investment. The Greens oppose privatisation, supporting the NHS Reinstatement Bill. Social care would receive £20 billion annually, introducing free personal care modelled on Scotland's system. Mental health services would achieve parity with physical health, with therapy accessible within 28 days.

## Housing

The party would build 150,000 social homes annually, ending right-to-buy. Local authorities would gain powers to implement rent controls and end no-fault evictions. A £29 billion programme would retrofit homes for energy efficiency, reducing bills and emissions.

## Workers' Rights and Welfare

Anti-union legislation since 1979 would be repealed, replaced by a Charter of Workers' Rights. A £15 minimum wage regardless of age, 10:1 maximum pay ratios, and movement toward a four-day week are proposed. Universal Credit would increase by £40 weekly, the two-child cap abolished, and disability benefits raised 5%.

## Democracy and Rights

The manifesto advocates proportional representation, votes at 16, abolishing voter ID requirements, and replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber. Human rights protections would be defended, protest rights restored, and trans self-identification supported.

## International Affairs

The Greens call for an immediate bilateral ceasefire in Gaza, Palestinian state recognition, and ending UK arms exports to Israel. They support rejoining the EU, signing the UN nuclear weapons prohibition treaty, and cancelling Trident. Overseas aid would rise to 1% of GNI.

Throughout, the Greens argue that climate solutions address inequality simultaneously—warmer homes, cleaner air, better jobs, and stronger communities emerge from the same transformative investments.
